source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: Mercury, common; since in his matutine position he is diurnal, but nocturnal when vespertine.

calculation_dependencies: Sun-relative position and source-defined matutine or vespertine status
normalized_rule: Mercury is common in this sect scheme: classify it as diurnal in a matutine position and nocturnal in a vespertine position.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sect classification, not a complete universal sect implementation.
review_notes: The main text calls Mercury common and makes the diurnal/nocturnal branch depend on matutine/vespertine position. Footnote 31 in the Ashmand edition, introduced as Whalley's note, adds chart-hemisphere qualifications; do not silently turn the main-text statement into a universal rule.
transmission_notes: The cited main text states Mercury's common and position-based sect. Footnote 31 in the Ashmand edition is explicitly introduced as Whalley's note and supplies the chart-hemisphere qualification; it is retained as editorial transmission context, not as Ptolemy's main text. Certainty is confidence in this Ashmand/Proclus transmission, not in an autograph of Ptolemy.
